scope.flow: _matchIncomingOrder quote-denominated fill order matching with lot-size flooring
scope.environment: CLOB.sol on-chain order matching (bid and ask loops)

statements.text: The incoming fill order is quote-denominated (amountIsBase = false).
A lot-size constraint is present (e.g., lotSizeInBase = 1e18) such that lot-size flooring can reduce the tradeable base amount.
The taker order has remaining quote amount (e.g., 2.5e18 quote units) and the maker has base liquidity (e.g., 3e18 base).
The order is a Fill-or-Kill order.
_matchIncomingOrder matches the quote-denominated fill order against maker liquidity, computing matchedBase, baseDelta via lot-size flooring, and quoteDelta.
The matching loop decrements the incoming order's remaining amount using matchedAmount in the bid and ask loops.
The FOK validation check is performed on newOrder.amount.

When baseDelta != matchedBase due to lot-size flooring, matchedAmount is set to takerOrder.amount (full remaining quote) instead of quoteDelta (actual quote consumed), over-subtracting and terminating the loop prematurely.
A Fill-or-Kill order must either execute completely or fail entirely; it must not be marked fully filled while any quote amount remains unfilled.

For a quote-denominated fill order, the order's remaining amount should be decremented only by the quote amount actually consumed (quoteDelta), so the order continues matching until its quote amount is filled.
The FOK check passes because newOrder.amount was incorrectly reduced to 0 even though dust quote amount remains unfilled, so the order is marked fully filled despite only partial execution.
Users receive fewer base tokens than their quote amount should purchase, since settlement uses the smaller quoteDelta and baseDelta values.
In the example, the order amount is reduced by 2.5 units while only 2 units worth of base tokens are traded, resulting in a 20% loss of expected value.
The matching loop terminates prematurely, preventing the order from continuing to match against additional liquidity.

ambiguities: Report does not state who calls _matchIncomingOrder or any authorization condition; no unauthorized-caller claim is made.
The FOK validation check's exact condition is not quoted in the fragments; only that it passes on newOrder.amount reduced to 0.
Whether the 20% loss figure generalizes beyond the single worked example is not established.
Report says bug affects all quote-denominated fill orders with lot-size constraints but provides no additional distinct effects beyond those extracted.
